title: Validate and normalize signup data
summary: A registration endpoint needs predictable, safe input before it creates an account. Validate and normalize the supplied signup fields, returning the structured result and field errors defined by the exercise. Validate an incoming signup payload without touching a database or an HTTP framework.
requirements: Input is an object { email, password, displayName }, all strings.
Trim and lowercase email; consider it valid if it matches the simplified pattern ^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$.
Password must be at least 8 characters (JavaScript string length); do not trim it.
Display name after trimming must contain between 2 and 40 characters inclusive.
Return { ok: false, errors: string[] } for invalid inputs, with error labels in order: email, password, displayName.
For valid input return { ok: true, user: { email: normalizedEmail, displayName: trimmedName } }.
Never include password in the output.
hints: Normalize the email and display name before checking their rules.
Collect all validation errors rather than returning on the first one.
Build the successful user object without copying the password.
